orogen_v3_temp_albedo_lat.label: Temp albedo lat
orogen_v3_temp_albedo_lat.description: North 1975 P2 albedo term (0.2 incl. ice)

orogen_v3_temp_albedo_snow.label: Temp albedo snow
orogen_v3_temp_albedo_snow.description: snow-covered forest ≈ 0.2–0.35, open snow 0.6–0.8; seasonal snow is patchy

orogen_v3_temp_land_heat_cap.label: Temp land heat cap
orogen_v3_temp_land_heat_cap.description: ≈ 2 m water equivalent (air column + top soil)

orogen_v3_temp_diffusivity_ew.label: Temp diffusivity ew
orogen_v3_temp_diffusivity_ew.description: eddy heat flux is mainly meridional (v′T′ ≫ u′T′); east–west exchange by the mean winds

orogen_v3_temp_wind_carry.label: Temp wind carry
orogen_v3_temp_wind_carry.description: share of the air column's heat the (near-surface) wind carries; no direct literature value — bounded by the whole column moving at about the surface wind

orogen_v3_temp_inversion_c.label: Temp inversion c
orogen_v3_temp_inversion_c.description: Arctic winter surface inversions ≈ 10–15 K (Serreze et al. 1992); strongest in the dark over snow

orogen_v3_temp_inversion_wind.label: Temp inversion wind
orogen_v3_temp_inversion_wind.description: stable boundary layers break down above ≈ 5–7 m/s near-surface wind

orogen_v3_temp_plateau_lapse.label: Temp plateau lapse
orogen_v3_temp_plateau_lapse.description: near-surface lapse rates over large elevated terrain ≈ 4.5–5.5 °C/km (elevated heating)

orogen_v3_temp_block_km.label: Temp block km
orogen_v3_temp_block_km.description: the marine / boundary layer a range must lift the air out of is ≈ 1–2 km deep; cold-air damming and blocked flow below ridge height (Froude < 1)

orogen_v3_temp_local_k.label: Temp local k
orogen_v3_temp_local_k.description: advective exchange of a ~1.5 km boundary layer at ~5 m/s over ~1000 km: ρ c_p H U / L ≈ 9 W/m²/K

orogen_v3_temp_current_memory.label: Temp current memory
orogen_v3_temp_current_memory.description: western boundary currents run ≈ 2–5 °C warmer and eastern boundary currents ≈ 2–4 °C colder than their latitude (OISST) — against ≈ 6–10 °C of latitude temperature change along ≈ 1500 km of their path

orogen_v3_temp_coast_carry.label: Temp coast carry
orogen_v3_temp_coast_carry.description: onshore winds carry the sea's warmth or cold a few hundred km inland (the maritime west coasts; the cool coastal deserts beside cold currents)

orogen_v3_temp_air_sea_days.label: Temp air sea days
orogen_v3_temp_air_sea_days.description: air-mass transformation over the sea: cold-air outbreaks warm ≈ 5–10 K within a day over open water (heat fluxes of 200–500 W/m² into a ≈ 1 km boundary layer)

orogen_v3_temp_air_sun_days.label: Temp air sun days
orogen_v3_temp_air_sun_days.description: a sunlit convective boundary layer (1–2 km) takes on its surface's heating within a day or two (sensible heat 100–300 W/m²)

orogen_v3_temp_air_dark_days.label: Temp air dark days
orogen_v3_temp_air_dark_days.description: maritime air over snowy winter continents cools ≈ 1–2 K/day (radiative loss from a stable boundary layer): a 10–20 K contrast lasts about a week — Atlantic air keeps Europe mild 2000–3000 km inland

orogen_v3_temp_local_km.label: Temp local km
orogen_v3_temp_local_km.description: the scale of the weather systems whose heat transport the diffusion stands for (≈ 1000–2000 km)

orogen_v3_temp_evap_damping.label: Temp evap damping
orogen_v3_temp_evap_damping.description: sensitivity of the surface latent heat flux to temperature ≈ 10–20 W/m²/K over tropical oceans and wet land (e.g. Hartmann 2016; Zhang & McPhaden 1995)

orogen_v3_temp_wet_cool_c.label: Temp wet cool c
orogen_v3_temp_wet_cool_c.description: soil-moisture–temperature coupling: dry soils raise monthly mean temperature by several K (Seneviratne et al. 2010); Sahel pre-monsoon vs monsoon months ≈ 5–6 K; tropical deforestation +1–3 K

orogen_v3_temp_sea_swing.label: Temp sea swing
orogen_v3_temp_sea_swing.description: mid-latitude sea-surface seasonal range ≈ 5–10 °C vs ≈ 20–40 °C over continents

orogen_v3_temp_albedo_vary.label: Temp albedo vary
orogen_v3_temp_albedo_vary.description: regional variation of surface and cloud albedo about the zonal mean ≈ ±0.02–0.05 (ERBE / CERES clear-sky and all-sky maps)

orogen_v3_temp_albedo_vary_km.label: Temp albedo vary km
orogen_v3_temp_albedo_vary_km.description: the size of regional albedo anomalies (deserts, forests, cloud decks) ≈ 500–2000 km

orogen_v3_temp_cloud_albedo.label: Temp cloud albedo
orogen_v3_temp_cloud_albedo.description: shortwave cloud forcing over land ≈ −50 to −100 W/m² under persistent rain clouds, ≈ 0 over deserts (CERES): an albedo contrast ≈ 0.1–0.25

orogen_v3_temp_cloud_lw_cancel.label: Temp cloud lw cancel
orogen_v3_temp_cloud_lw_cancel.description: deep tropical convection: shortwave cloud forcing ≈ −100 W/m² nearly cancelled by longwave ≈ +90 W/m² (Kiehl 1994; Hartmann et al. 2001; ERBE/CERES)

orogen_v3_temp_ice_lapse.label: Temp ice lapse
orogen_v3_temp_ice_lapse.description: Antarctic ice-sheet surface temperature vs height ≈ 8 K/km (Fortuin & Oerlemans 1990)

orogen_v3_temp_ice_dome_km.label: Temp ice dome km
orogen_v3_temp_ice_dome_km.description: mean surface elevation of ice sheets ≈ 2.1 km (Greenland) and 2.3 km (Antarctica); small ice caps less

orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_grow.label: Temp sea ice grow
orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_grow.description: thin sea ice grows ≈ 1–3 cm/day at −10 °C (Stefan / Lebedev: h ≈ 1.33·FDD^0.58 cm)

orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_stefan_m.label: Temp sea ice stefan m
orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_stefan_m.description: first-year ice reaches ≈ 1–2 m after a winter of 2000–5000 °C·days (Lebedev 1938; Maykut 1986)

orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_melt.label: Temp sea ice melt
orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_melt.description: summer surface melt ≈ 0.5–1.5 m over a season of a few hundred positive degree-days (Perovich et al. 2003)

orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_h0.label: Temp sea ice h0
orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_h0.description: ice ≈ 0.3–1 m thick closes the sea (consolidated pack vs new ice and leads)

orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_spread_km.label: Temp sea ice spread km
orogen_v3_temp_sea_ice_spread_km.description: sea-ice drift ≈ 5–10 km/day — a few hundred to a thousand km over a season (IABP buoys)

orogen_v3_temp_polar_summer_damp.label: Temp polar summer damp
orogen_v3_temp_polar_summer_damp.description: Arctic summers: the surface stays near 0 °C while snow and sea ice melt, and the July 10 °C isotherm (the tree line) lies near 65–72°N on every continent; land poleward of 75° is tundra or ice everywhere on Earth (Beck et al. 2023). No direct value — set so the model's 66–80°N summers match, winters untouched

orogen_v3_temp_ice_start_c.label: Temp ice start c
orogen_v3_temp_ice_start_c.description: ice-sheet hysteresis: once grown, polar ice sheets persist under climates that would not grow them (e.g. DeConto & Pollard 2003; Abe-Ouchi et al. 2013)

orogen_v3_circ_hadley_scale.label: Circ hadley scale
orogen_v3_circ_hadley_scale.description: Held & Hou 1980 underestimates the observed Hadley edge by ~20 % (e.g. Frierson et al. 2007)

orogen_v3_circ_hadley_seasonal.label: Circ hadley seasonal
orogen_v3_circ_hadley_seasonal.description: observed subtropical highs migrate ≈ 10° with the rain belt (NCEP); Held & Hou per month would cancel it; seasonal Hadley cells are not in equilibrium with each month (Lindzen & Hou 1988)

orogen_v3_circ_tropical_hpa.label: Circ tropical hpa
orogen_v3_circ_tropical_hpa.description: zonal-mean sea-level pressure ≈ 1009 hPa in the rain belt vs ≈ 1018 in the subtropical highs

orogen_v3_circ_midlat_hpa.label: Circ midlat hpa
orogen_v3_circ_midlat_hpa.description: zonal-mean sea-level pressure over the Southern Ocean: ≈ 1018 hPa at 35°S to ≈ 987 at 65°S, both seasons (NCEP)

orogen_v3_circ_open_sea_power.label: Circ open sea power
orogen_v3_circ_open_sea_power.description: the land-broken northern belt (≈ 45 % sea) has a zonal-mean trough of only ≈ 6 hPa in both seasons vs ≈ 30 over the ≈ 93 % sea south (NCEP): (0.45/0.93)^p ≈ 1/5

orogen_v3_circ_polar_hpa.label: Circ polar hpa
orogen_v3_circ_polar_hpa.description: polar highs a few hPa above the subpolar troughs

orogen_v3_circ_heat_low_mild.label: Circ heat low mild
orogen_v3_circ_heat_low_mild.description: heat lows are deep (≈ 10 hPa) over hot, dry interiors with a 3–5 km boundary layer and weak over mild, moist land (summer Europe: the Azores ridge, not a low; NCEP)

orogen_v3_circ_heat_low_tropics.label: Circ heat low tropics
orogen_v3_circ_heat_low_tropics.description: the deep heat lows sit in the dry subtropics (Sahara ≈ 25°N, Pakistan ≈ 30°N, Pilbara ≈ 21°S, Kalahari ≈ 20°S), not over the convective wet tropics (NCEP)

orogen_v3_circ_ocean_high_hpa.label: Circ ocean high hpa
orogen_v3_circ_ocean_high_hpa.description: winter subtropical highs over the oceans (Azores ≈ 1024 hPa at 35°N) vs the land beside them (Sahara ≈ 1018): ≈ 6–8 hPa across ≈ ±0.5 of sea share (NCEP)

orogen_v3_circ_heat_low_hot.label: Circ heat low hot
orogen_v3_circ_heat_low_hot.description: heat lows over hot deserts reach 10–20 hPa below the latitude mean (Pakistan ≈ 996 hPa in July): the heated boundary layer is 3–5 km deep, several times that over mild land or sea (NCEP)

orogen_v3_circ_cold_high_boost.label: Circ cold high boost
orogen_v3_circ_cold_high_boost.description: cold anticyclones strengthen as the surface inversion deepens over very cold snow (Siberian high ≈ 1035 hPa at −30 °C)

orogen_v3_circ_thermal_hpa_per_k.label: Circ thermal hpa per k
orogen_v3_circ_thermal_hpa_per_k.description: hydrostatic: warming the lowest 2–3 km by 1 K lowers surface pressure ≈ 0.9–1.3 hPa

orogen_v3_circ_trough_max_lat.label: Circ trough max lat
orogen_v3_circ_trough_max_lat.description: the summer monsoon trough joins the heat lows of Pakistan and Tibet (≈ 28–35°N), the Sahara (≈ 20–25°N), Arizona (≈ 33°N), the Pilbara (≈ 22°S) (NCEP)

orogen_v3_circ_trough_high_deg.label: Circ trough high deg
orogen_v3_circ_trough_high_deg.description: over a summer continent the subtropical ridge lies poleward of the heat low (the Tibetan High aloft and the westerlies beyond ≈ 40°N in July)

orogen_v3_circ_monsoon_hpa_per_k.label: Circ monsoon hpa per k
orogen_v3_circ_monsoon_hpa_per_k.description: summer monsoon troughs below the rain belt (≈ 1010 hPa): South Asia ≈ 996–1000 hPa over a ≈ 10 K heat low (Tibet heating the air aloft), the Sahara ≈ 1008 over ≈ 3 K (NCEP July)

orogen_v3_circ_rossby_km.label: Circ rossby km
orogen_v3_circ_rossby_km.description: Rossby radius of deformation ≈ 1000 km in midlatitudes

orogen_v3_circ_turn_ocean_deg.label: Circ turn ocean deg
orogen_v3_circ_turn_ocean_deg.description: surface wind crosses isobars at ≈ 10–20° over the sea

orogen_v3_circ_surface_wind.label: Circ surface wind
orogen_v3_circ_surface_wind.description: near-surface wind ≈ 0.6–0.8 of the geostrophic wind over the sea

orogen_v3_circ_surface_wind_land.label: Circ surface wind land
orogen_v3_circ_surface_wind_land.description: 10 m wind over land ≈ 0.4–0.6 of the geostrophic wind (roughness)

orogen_v3_ocean_friction.label: Ocean friction
orogen_v3_ocean_friction.description: Stommel layer width r/β should span ≈ 2 grid cells (MITgcm guidance); ≈ 300 km at 2°

orogen_v3_ocean_gust_ms.label: Ocean gust ms
orogen_v3_ocean_gust_ms.description: bulk formulas on climatological winds add a gustiness / synoptic speed of a few m/s

orogen_v3_ocean_channel_drag.label: Ocean channel drag
orogen_v3_ocean_channel_drag.description: sets a circumpolar current of ≈ 100–150 Sv on Earth (the ACC)

orogen_v3_ocean_heat_share.label: Ocean heat share
orogen_v3_ocean_heat_share.description: scaled to the ocean's ≈ 1–2 PW poleward heat transport; no direct literature value

orogen_v3_ocean_overturn_pw.label: Ocean overturn pw
orogen_v3_ocean_overturn_pw.description: Atlantic meridional overturning heat transport ≈ 1.2 PW at 26°N (RAPID array), released in the subpolar and Nordic seas

orogen_v3_ocean_merid_share.label: Ocean merid share
orogen_v3_ocean_merid_share.description: western boundary currents release ≈ 100–200 W/m² (Gulf Stream, Kuroshio), eastern boundary currents take up ≈ 20–50 W/m² plus upwelling (Yu & Weller 2007 OAFlux); the gyres carry ≈ 1 PW poleward

orogen_v3_ocean_upwell_dt.label: Ocean upwell dt
orogen_v3_ocean_upwell_dt.description: upwelling under a shallow thermocline cools the surface 5–10 °C below its latitude (Peru, Benguela, the east Pacific cold tongue)

orogen_v3_ocean_thermo_east_m.label: Ocean thermo east m
orogen_v3_ocean_thermo_east_m.description: the thermocline at the eastern ocean margins ≈ 30–60 m deep (east Pacific, Benguela)

orogen_v3_ocean_thermo_scale_m.label: Ocean thermo scale m
orogen_v3_ocean_thermo_scale_m.description: the warm pool's thermocline ≈ 150–200 m deep: upwelling there barely cools the surface (Bjerknes; McPhaden & Picaut 1990)

orogen_v3_ocean_thermo_eq_m.label: Ocean thermo eq m
orogen_v3_ocean_thermo_eq_m.description: the equatorial thermocline (20 °C isotherm) ≈ 150–200 m deep in the west Pacific, ≈ 50 m in the east: a mean ≈ 100–120 m

orogen_v3_ocean_shore_km.label: Ocean shore km
orogen_v3_ocean_shore_km.description: islands smaller than a few deformation radii (≈ 100–300 km) barely block the planetary waves that set the thermocline

orogen_v3_ocean_gprime.label: Ocean gprime
orogen_v3_ocean_gprime.description: reduced gravity of the tropical thermocline ≈ 0.02–0.04 m/s² (Δρ/ρ ≈ 0.002–0.004)

orogen_v3_ocean_eq_deg.label: Ocean eq deg
orogen_v3_ocean_eq_deg.description: the equatorial Rossby radius ≈ 300 km ≈ 3°; the zonal tilt holds within ≈ 5–8° of the equator

orogen_v3_ocean_ekman_tauy_deg.label: Ocean ekman tauy deg
orogen_v3_ocean_ekman_tauy_deg.description: Ekman balance fails within ≈ 3–5° of the equator; there a meridional stress drives a downwind, not a zonal, drift (Zebiak & Cane 1987; Philander & Pacanowski 1981)

orogen_v3_ocean_coast_land_share.label: Ocean coast land share
orogen_v3_ocean_coast_land_share.description: coastal upwelling needs a coast long compared with the deformation radius (Allen 1980; island wakes and island upwelling are weak and local)

orogen_v3_ocean_coast_km.label: Ocean coast km
orogen_v3_ocean_coast_km.description: coastal upwelling zones and their filaments reach ≈ 100–300 km offshore (California, Peru, Benguela)

orogen_v3_ocean_season_scale.label: Ocean season scale
orogen_v3_ocean_season_scale.description: the wind-driven gyres' seasonal cycle: large in the tropics (the Somali Current reverses with the monsoon; the equatorial countercurrent swells and ebbs), small in the subtropical gyres (Schott & McCreary 2001)

orogen_v3_ocean_season_full_deg.label: Ocean season full deg
orogen_v3_ocean_season_full_deg.description: equatorial Kelvin and Rossby waves cross a basin in weeks to months: the tropical ocean follows the seasons

orogen_v3_ocean_season_zero_deg.label: Ocean season zero deg
orogen_v3_ocean_season_zero_deg.description: midlatitude Rossby waves take years to cross a basin, so the gyres there hold their annual-mean state (developer: fade out by ≈ 60°)

orogen_v3_rain_evap_coeff.label: Rain evap coeff
orogen_v3_rain_evap_coeff.description: bulk transfer coefficient C_E ≈ 1.1–1.5 × 10⁻³ (Large & Pond 1982; COARE)

orogen_v3_rain_surface_rh.label: Rain surface rh
orogen_v3_rain_surface_rh.description: near-surface relative humidity over the oceans ≈ 75–80 %

orogen_v3_rain_terrain_height_km.label: Rain terrain height km
orogen_v3_rain_terrain_height_km.description: precipitable water over the Tibetan Plateau (h ≈ 4.5–5 km) ≈ 20–25 % of the Indian lowlands’ in summer: e-folding ≈ 3–3.5 km averaged over the plateau, more where it is most heated (the elevated heated surface keeps a deep moist boundary layer)

orogen_v3_rain_timescale_h.label: Rain timescale h
orogen_v3_rain_timescale_h.description: Bretherton et al. 2004: P = exp(15.6 (r − 0.603)) mm/day ⇒ a saturated tropical column rains out in ≈ 3 h

orogen_v3_rain_rh_steepness.label: Rain rh steepness
orogen_v3_rain_rh_steepness.description: Bretherton et al. 2004 (15.6), from satellite column water and rain over the tropical oceans

orogen_v3_rain_eddy_diff.label: Rain eddy diff
orogen_v3_rain_eddy_diff.description: tropical transients (easterly waves, convection) mix far less than mid-latitude storms; no direct literature value

orogen_v3_rain_eddy_length_km.label: Rain eddy length km
orogen_v3_rain_eddy_length_km.description: mixing length ≈ the size of the storms (Rossby radius ≈ 1000 km); gives K ≈ 1–3 × 10⁶ m²/s in the storm belts (Frierson et al. 2007: 1.06 × 10⁶ m²/s for moist static energy)

orogen_v3_rain_tropical_rh.label: Rain tropical rh
orogen_v3_rain_tropical_rh.description: monsoon depressions and easterly waves form in the monsoon troughs' cyclonic shear (≈ 1–3 × 10⁻⁵ s⁻¹) and bring ≈ 40–50 % of central and north India's monsoon rain (Hurley & Boos 2015); no direct value for the humidity spread; the derived winds are smooth, their cyclonic vorticity ≈ 5 × 10⁻⁶ s⁻¹, so the coefficient is larger than the shear alone would give

orogen_v3_rain_tropical_km.label: Rain tropical km
orogen_v3_rain_tropical_km.description: monsoon depressions and easterly waves ≈ 1000–2000 km across

orogen_v3_rain_storm_rh.label: Rain storm rh
orogen_v3_rain_storm_rh.description: sub-monthly spread of column relative humidity ≈ 0.1–0.2 in the storm belts, where the Eady growth rate is ≈ 0.6–0.8 per day; no direct literature value

orogen_v3_rain_wind_rot.label: Rain wind rot
orogen_v3_rain_wind_rot.description: the moisture-weighted wind (≈ 900 hPa) is close to the wind above the friction layer

orogen_v3_rain_wind_div_dry.label: Rain wind div dry
orogen_v3_rain_wind_div_dry.description: shallow (≈ 1 km) convergence of heat lows and trade-wind divergence: ≈ 30–40 % of the column’s water (scale height ≈ 2.5 km)

orogen_v3_rain_wind_div_moist.label: Rain wind div moist
orogen_v3_rain_wind_div_moist.description: rain-belt inflow ≈ 1.5–3 km deep: moisture convergence ≈ 0.5–0.7 × W × surface convergence (P − E ≈ 5–10 mm/day)

orogen_v3_rain_stability.label: Rain stability
orogen_v3_rain_stability.description: rain is suppressed under strong low inversions (cold upwelling, stratocumulus decks; Klein & Hartmann 1993: low cloud +6 %/K of stability); no direct literature value

orogen_v3_rain_terrain_heat_k.label: Rain terrain heat k
orogen_v3_rain_terrain_heat_k.description: a deep convective boundary layer (2–4 km) forms over strongly heated high ground (Tibet, pre-monsoon and monsoon); over cold or snowy high ground the boundary layer is shallow and stable

orogen_v3_rain_high_k_per_hpa.label: Rain high k per hpa
orogen_v3_rain_high_k_per_hpa.description: subsidence under the subtropical highs warms the air above the marine layer by several K (a trade-wind / stratocumulus inversion of 5–10 K under +5–10 hPa highs)

orogen_v3_rain_instability.label: Rain instability
orogen_v3_rain_instability.description: convection over surfaces warmer than their surroundings (heated plateaus, warm currents such as the Gulf Stream and Kuroshio) raises rain for the same humidity; no direct literature value — kept to the scale of the stable-air term

orogen_v3_rain_stable_ref_km.label: Rain stable ref km
orogen_v3_rain_stable_ref_km.description: the free troposphere over a surface is set by its air mass over ≈ 1000–2000 km (the Rossby radius), not by the latitude circle: Siberian winter air is cold aloft too

orogen_v3_rain_front_mm.label: Rain front mm
orogen_v3_rain_front_mm.description: frontal cyclones bring 30–60 mm/month to mid-latitude continental interiors at 45–60° (eastern Europe, the Canadian prairies, the Russian plain) well beyond the reach of the mean flow; the polar-front band of Worldbuilding Pasta

orogen_v3_rain_front_pos.label: Rain front pos
orogen_v3_rain_front_pos.description: the polar-front jet and storm track ≈ 40°N in winter and 50–55°N in summer, about midway between the subtropical high and the subpolar low

orogen_v3_rain_front_deg.label: Rain front deg
orogen_v3_rain_front_deg.description: the storm track ≈ 15–25° of latitude wide

orogen_v3_rain_front_high_hpa.label: Rain front high hpa
orogen_v3_rain_front_high_hpa.description: fronts steer around blocking and subtropical highs (a few hPa above the zonal mean)

orogen_v3_rain_soil_mm.label: Rain soil mm
orogen_v3_rain_soil_mm.description: plant-available soil water capacity ≈ 100–200 mm (e.g. Manabe 1969 bucket: 150 mm)

orogen_v3_rain_land_convection.label: Rain land convection
orogen_v3_rain_land_convection.description: daytime convection over wet land: rain over land peaks in the afternoon and picks up at ≈ 5–10 % lower column humidity than over the sea (Schiro et al. 2016; Bergemann & Jakob 2016); soil-moisture–precipitation coupling in monsoon regions (Koster et al. 2004)

orogen_v3_rain_column_local.label: Rain column local
orogen_v3_rain_column_local.description: lower-tropospheric temperature anomalies over continents are ≈ 40–60 % of the surface anomaly

orogen_v3_rain_orog_storm.label: Rain orog storm
orogen_v3_rain_orog_storm.description: orographic precipitation is concentrated in storms with strong cross-barrier flow (≈ 10–20 m/s), not the weak monthly-mean wind (Roe 2005)

orogen_v3_rain_lee_per_km.label: Rain lee per km
orogen_v3_rain_lee_per_km.description: lee-side rain falls ≈ ×0.2–0.5 of windward within a few hundred km behind 1–2 km of relief (Cascades, Andes, Southern Alps; Roe 2005)

orogen_v3_rain_lee_recover_km.label: Rain lee recover km
orogen_v3_rain_lee_recover_km.description: rain shadows extend a few hundred km downwind of major ranges (Great Basin, Patagonia, Tarim; Roe 2005)

orogen_v3_rain_rise_per_km.label: Rain rise per km
orogen_v3_rain_rise_per_km.description: windward precipitation grows ≈ 5–10 % per 100 m of elevation up to near the crest of mid-latitude ranges (Alps, Cascades, Sierra Nevada; Roe 2005)

orogen_v3_rain_island_boost.label: Rain island boost
orogen_v3_rain_island_boost.description: tropical islands receive ≈ 1.5–3× the rain of the surrounding ocean (sea-breeze convergence and orography; e.g. the Maritime Continent, Hawaii, the Caribbean)

orogen_v3_rain_orog_spread_km.label: Rain orog spread km
orogen_v3_rain_orog_spread_km.description: water wrung out on the windward side is missing downwind — the rain-shadow budget closes over a few hundred km

orogen_v3_rain_slope_factor.label: Rain slope factor
orogen_v3_rain_slope_factor.description: orographic enhancement ≈ ×2–3 on windward slopes, ×0.3–0.6 in the lee at ≈ 0.1–0.2 m/s of forced ascent in storms (Roe 2005; Smith & Barstad 2004); moved within the spread distance, not made

orogen_v3_rain_orographic.label: Rain orographic
orogen_v3_rain_orographic.description: precipitation efficiency of orographic clouds ≈ 20–50 % (Jiang & Smith 2003)
